references.text: God completed his work on the seventh day and rested. He blessed the seventh day and made it holy, which forms the basis for the Sabbath commandment.
The people of Israel receive instructions to keep the Sabbath in connection with the gathering of manna, before the law was given at Sinai.
The Sabbath is described as a sign between God and the people of Israel for all generations, and it is emphasized that it must be kept holy.
Moses repeats the Sabbath commandment to the people and emphasizes that no work should be done on the seventh day.
A parallel presentation of the Sabbath commandment in Deuteronomy, with an extended reason linked to deliverance from Egypt.
Isaiah speaks about the blessing for those who keep the Sabbath and do not profane it.
Isaiah describes how one should honor the Sabbath, calling it a delight, and promises blessing to those who keep it.
Ezekiel reminds that God gave Israel the Sabbaths as a sign between himself and them, so that they would know that he is the Lord who sanctifies them.
Nehemiah rebukes the people for profaning the Sabbath by engaging in trade, and reminds them to keep the Sabbath day holy.
Jesus teaches that the Sabbath was made for man's sake, and that the Son of Man is lord of the Sabbath.
Jesus heals a woman on the Sabbath and teaches about the true meaning of the Sabbath.
The book of Hebrews speaks of a Sabbath rest waiting for God's people, linking it to God's rest after creation.
A retelling of the same message in Deuteronomy with emphasis on obedience to the original command.
Expands the message by highlighting the consequences of breaking it and underscores the holy character of the Sabbath as a vital boundary.
Reveals the deepest purpose of the Sabbath: a sign of the covenant and identity between God and his people.
Links Sabbath observance directly to reverence for God's presence and the sanctuary.
Provides the historical basis: the Sabbath is a reminder of deliverance from slavery.
Confirms that obedience to the Sabbath is the foundation of the relationship with God and the sanctuary.
Clarifies what 'keeping the day holy' means in practice by forbidding work and carrying burdens.
